title: A Choir for the Ember
premise: Astrid Eriksen, a beast-speaker who has spent her life hiding the gift that got her mother burned, guides smugglers through the Thornfell mountains until a chance meeting with Wren Calloway—a scholar hunting a century-old book of prophecies—reveals their first date already written in its pages. The prophecy names them both as the ones who must reach the Ember, the last dragon-fire beneath Thornfell's crown-city, before it gutters out and frees the thing that has worn King Aldric like a puppet for thirty years. As Astrid and Wren fall in love against every law forbidding her gift and his heresy, they gather a ragged found family of smugglers, exiled priests, and talking beasts to unbind the king from the crown-thing Vaskr. In the end Astrid must speak with the Ember itself—trading her own memories of Wren as the price—and though she forgets him, the family they built remembers for her, and love begins again on the mountain road where they first met.
about_author: Xanthe Eastwick is a former choir singer turned fantasy novelist who grew up in a Norwegian fishing village and now writes from a drafty attic in Edinburgh. Her work is known for warm found-family ensembles, folklore-steeped mountains, and love stories that cost something.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She leads a smuggling caravan through Thornfell's passes, quietly bargaining with wolves and ravens whose speech no one else can hear, hiding her gift even from her crew. When a rockslide traps them, she uses her gift openly for one desperate moment—and knows someone saw. Emotional beat: the loneliness of constant concealment.

chapters.title: A Date, Written Down
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The young scholar Wren Calloway arrives in the border town chasing rumors of the Codex of Ash, a prophetic book sealed a century ago. He collides—literally—with Astrid at a tavern, and they agree to meet tomorrow. That night he finds the Codex and reads an account of tonight's meeting, word for word. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ink That Knows Your Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Wren shows Astrid the page: their date is prophecy, and so is their deaths unless they 'reach the Ember before it gutters.' Astrid wants to burn the book; Wren wants to follow it. A raven warns Astrid that the king's hunters are coming for a beast-speaker. Beat: reluctant alliance forged by fear.

chapters.title: What the Wolves Remember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Fleeing town, Astrid consults an old wolf-pack whose matriarch remembers the last dragon-fire dimming. The wolf speaks of Vaskr, the thing in the crown, and of a price the Ember always exacts: a memory freely given. Beat: Astrid learns what the quest may cost her and tells no one.

chapters.title: The Company of the Crooked Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They gather allies: Halvard, Astrid's gruff smuggler captain with a soft heart; Sister Maren, a priest exiled for heresy about the crown; and Pip, a pickpocket child who talks to goats almost as well as Astrid talks to everything. Beat: the found family assembles around a campfire, laughing despite doom.

chapters.title: Hunters in White Coats
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The king's Purifiers ambush the company at a river ford; Astrid reveals her gift publicly, turning a bear to their defense, and saves them but marks herself forever. Wren sees her fully for the first time and is not afraid. Beat: love kindling in the aftermath of violence.

chapters.title: The City Under the Crown
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The company infiltrates the capital, Crownspire, where King Aldric parades hollow-eyed through streets of forced celebration. Maren explains the theology of binding: Vaskr feeds on the Ember, and the Ember dims nightly. Beat: dread deepens; the enemy has a face and it smiles.

chapters.title: Choir of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Hiding in the undercity, Pip befriends the rats, pigeons, and gutter-cats, who form a surveillance network for the company. Through them Astrid learns the palace's secret ways. Beat: warmth and humor—the smallest members prove mighty.

chapters.title: The Page That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Codex updates itself, now describing events hours before they happen—including Astrid's capture. Wren tries to rewrite a page and his hands burn. He confesses he may have been chosen not to help but to witness. Beat: guilt, and Astrid forgiving him before he finishes apologizing.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Last Warning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On a rooftop above the frozen city, Astrid and Wren finally kiss—and the Codex, miles away, writes the kiss down before it happens, proving their love was foretold too. Astrid wonders if anything she feels is truly hers. Beat: tenderness shadowed by fatalism.

chapters.title: The Purifier's Net
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. The prophecy fulfills itself: Astrid is captured by Purifiers led by Inquisitor Solveig, who once loved Astrid's mother. Halvard chooses loyalty over profit and turns the smugglers' fleet toward rescue. Beat: betrayal averted; family proven.

chapters.title: Cells of Quiet Fire
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Imprisoned beneath the palace, Astrid discovers the cells sit beside the dying Ember itself, and hears its voice—ancient, grieving, nearly gone. It tells her the truth: Vaskr was once the king's twin brother, bound by a bargain Aldric regrets. Beat: the enemy reframed as tragedy.

chapters.title: The Hollow King Speaks
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV (a single chapter inside the king). For one hour each night the binding thins and Aldric wakes inside his own body, aware of everything Vaskr does. He leaves a message for Astrid in beast-speech he learned from his dead wife. Beat: devastating sympathy for the monster's host.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Guttering
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The company—smugglers, priest, child, and an army of rats—breaches the prison during the Ember's weakest hour. Solveig, confronted with proof of Vaskr's nature, wavers and lets them pass. Beat: triumph laced with loss; Maren dies holding the door.

chapters.title: Ash and Covenant
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the Codex's final pages, Wren finds the ritual to unbind king from crown-thing—but also the price: the Ember demands a cherished memory, freely surrendered. He realizes Astrid learned this chapters ago and said nothing. Beat: anger, then understanding; he offers his own memory instead.

chapters.title: Vaskr Unmasked
chapters.summary: Solveig's POV. Vaskr, sensing the plot, sheds pretense and seizes the city, wearing Aldric's face while commanding Purifiers who finally see what they serve. Solveig defects, bringing the Purifiers' secret archive. Beat: open war in the streets; the stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Descent to the Ember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The company fights its way down through collapsing vaults to the Ember's chamber, where Vaskr waits, offering Astrid her mother's memory back if she betrays them. She refuses. Beat: temptation answered; resolve crystallized.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, ensemble POV. The ritual begins: Wren reads, Maren's heresy sung as a choir by smugglers, Solveig holding the line above. Vaskr tears free of Aldric mid-rite. Astrid speaks to the Ember directly and offers the memory it wants—not of her mother, but of Wren. Beat: sacrifice at full pitch.

chapters.title: What Was Given
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Freed, Aldric takes up his sword and burns Vaskr in the rekindled Ember, dying with it—the binding required a crowned life. The fire blazes whole again, taking Astrid's memories of Wren as payment. Beat: victory and grief entwined; the king redeemed.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Awake among her people, Astrid knows everyone except the kind scholar watching her with wet eyes. Wren keeps his promise not to tell her what she paid. She feels the shape of the absence and hates it. Beat: quiet devastation; love outliving memory.

chapters.title: Pages Written Forward
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Codex, its purpose served, begins writing blank pages instead of prophecies—except one last entry: a meeting on the mountain road, a year hence, between two strangers. Wren decides prophecy is just a promise someone kept. Beat: hope rekindled.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Ember
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, final chapter. One year later, the found family thrives in a free Crownspire; beasts and humans speak openly. On the mountain road, Astrid meets a traveling scholar and feels something old stir—her mother's stories say the heart keeps what the mind loses. She asks his name. Beat: resolution as beginning; love, remembered by everything except her, starts again.
